title: These Are the World's Most 'Welcoming' Cities
paragraphs: Which places in the world make travelers feel the most welcome? According to the travel booking company Booking.com, the answer is a small town in Italy.

Every year, Booking.com gives Traveller Review Awards to hotels, apartments and other places to stay that get very good reviews from guests. To win an award, a place must have an average guest score of at least 8 out of 10. The 2026 awards, which were announced in February 2026, were based on more than 370 million reviews. In total, about 1.8 million places to stay in 221 countries and territories won an award.
Booking.com also made a list of the world's "most welcoming" cities. To make the list, the company looked at which places had the largest share of places to stay that won an award.

Montepulciano, a small town in the Tuscany region of Italy, was first. It is famous for its wine and old buildings. Magong, in Taiwan, was second, and San Martín de los Andes, in Argentina, was third. The rest of the top 10 were Harrogate in the UK, Fredericksburg in Texas, Pirenópolis in Brazil, Swakopmund in Namibia, Takayama in Japan, Noosa Heads in Australia and Klaipeda in Lithuania.
Booking.com also made a list of the most welcoming regions. These included Hidalgo in Mexico, Newfoundland and Labrador in Canada, and Navarra in Spain.

Italy had the most award winners of any country, for the ninth year in a row. It had 214,666 winners. France and Spain came next. The number of winners also grew fast in some countries. It rose 68% in Bulgaria, 46% in South Korea, 39% in China and 29% in Japan. Apartments won more awards than any other type of accommodation, and the number of ryokan, traditional Japanese inns, that won awards rose 13%.
James Waters of Booking.com said that the awards "continue to shine a well-deserved spotlight on our partners."
